fact_list: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
The word “robot” comes from a 1920 Czech play, R.U.R.
Adults have 206 bones; babies have more, and some fuse together as they grow.
Footprints on the Moon can last a very long time — there is no wind or rain to wipe them away.
An ostrich’s eye is bigger than its brain.
An adult’s heart beats about 100,000 times a day.
Honeybees show each other the way to flowers by dancing.
Water expands when it freezes, which is why ice floats.
Mount Everest grows a few millimetres taller every year.

a11y.voice_input_hint: For parents: lets your child dictate the prompt. The browser transcribes the voice, often with a cloud service (e.g. Google), so this is off by default.

parents.reviews_hint: A short review at the right moment helps make it stick for good.
tips: Praise effort and strategy, not being “smart”: “You really thought that through.”
Ask them to explain it to you — teaching is the best way to learn.
Ten minutes a day beats an hour once a week.
A mistake is information, not failure: ask what they'd try differently next time.
